Decision — desktop theming and style

Status: accepted 2026-10-21. Amends egui applications, style tokens as data, scheme and style axes, the chrome family, session icon stroke and type, settings authority and settings summary reads. Settings contract 0.9.0 (additive), store format 4.

The decision

  • One look per process. An application installs its theme once with toolkit::install and reads every colour, length, radius, stroke and font back from the egui context. Nothing is threaded through view functions; no application sets an egui style, visuals or fonts itself.
  • Every painted or interacted number is a token, and later tokens are data. The style family's forty original tokens are the required set; every later token is defaulted from an append-only compatibility table when a design omits it, through an immutable fallback rule that covers every authored style name, so every sealed profile keeps compiling and adding a token never needs a store migration. There are no read-only values: the behaviour values (resize edges, scrub rates, hit tolerance, menu scroll speed, double-click time, the icon mask) are tokens with floors that keep the interaction possible.
  • Applications add no literal lengths and no literal colours.
  • Session tunables. The profile's tune maps style.<token> or chrome.<role> to a value, validated against a registry the design crate publishes and settings.describe lists; apps.<id>.tune does the same for one application; view.look.preview does it for one window. Style and chrome tunes therefore have session, application and window scope. Relations between tokens are constraints validated on the final layered values and refused with both sides named. Unknown and retired names in a stored record are kept and reported, never dropped; aliases are canonicalised within each layer. The design is never patched.
  • Resolution order: session axes, the application's own axis override, the window's choice; the profile's pinned design source compiled with its defaults; the legacy session choices (icon stroke, fonts); session tune; application tune; window preview; then accessibility (ui.reduced_motion zeroes animation). Every value reports its source and what it shadows. Legacy choices own their targets.
  • Every application compiles the profile's pinned design source. When the profile's source digest differs from the design the binary carries, the application fetches the source once with settings.source, verifies it by digest, caches it per user and compiles it; until it arrives the embedded design is drawn and reported. Custom design sources are therefore ordinary profiles: the session look, tunes and previews apply to them.
  • Tuned colours are exact and unchecked; writes warn below 4.5:1 and the look report marks them. The field focus border stays and its width and colour role are tokens.
  • Read, preview and choose over the Bus. Every application answers <app>.look and publishes <app>.look.changed: authority identity, the window's look generation, which source was compiled, axes, every token and role with value, default, source and shadowed layers, the egui slot each role owns, the fonts actually drawn, content regions with the palette they draw with. view.look.preview {tune, expect} is fenced on the authority's incarnation and revision and on the window's look generation, bounded, one per window, cleared by every look change except the arrival of the window's pinned design source, which keeps it. view.theme.set is the window's axis choice; older per-application theme verbs are deprecated aliases. Writes use settings.validate, settings.apply (fenced; null resets), settings.reset and prefs.appearance.set. Undo is the caller's held before-values applied as an inverse fenced on the accepted receipt.
  • One scroll bar. toolkit::scroll wraps egui's bar with the style's tokens; the handle takes the state's text colour at a resting opacity, the track shows only while hot. The document canvas keeps its own bars, from tokens.
  • One form row (toolkit::form) and one set of fields.
  • Chrome and content are two scopes. A light content region draws the window's design and overlays with only the mode forced to light; other regions inherit the window. The terminal's colours are a settings domain with session scope, terminal.colors: sixteen ANSI entries, foreground, background and cursor, each a colour or null for the design's default for the session's scheme and mode (the cursor default is a policy, invert or a colour); a running program's palette changes sit over them until reset; explicit RGB cells are drawn as sent.
  • The compositor's title bars follow each window's look. A server-decorated window's bar is drawn from that window's resolved look, read with <app>.look and refreshed on <app>.look.changed, so a window's own scheme choice and its preview show in its title bar. The window's application is attributed through the broker's own record of the service's connection, never through self-reported identity; a window the compositor cannot attribute, or an extra window of a multi-window application that carries no toplevel tag, draws the persistent session and application look. The wallpaper follows the same look.
  • Two new chrome schemes, breeze and adwaita, each light and dark, with their own styles and terminal colour tables; a design that lacks them takes them from the compatibility table.
  • Rollout and rollback. Every reader ships before settingsd writes the new fields; settingsd downgrade --to 3 --target <previous binary> checks eligibility in process and then with the previous binary itself on each candidate, and only then re-seals the store for it, primary first; it refuses otherwise, naming the reason.
  • Gates. Workspace clippy disallows the raw egui widgets, every style setter and theme threading by resolved path; legitimate uses outside applications carry an expect with a reason that fails when stale; tools/style_gate.mix refuses spacing and colour literals and unlisted constants in every application GUI crate, and holds the toolkit to its token inventory.

Why

A desktop is one surface. The tokens, the settings authority and the toolkit already exist; what leaked was the last mile inside each application, where a stroke was threaded by hand, a gap was a number and a scroll bar was whatever egui gave. Closing those leaks once, and letting a session tune any token over the Bus, means the next hundred style adjustments are data and a settings.apply, not a release and not a migration.

Consequences

  • Every application changes mechanically once; new knobs never need a schema field, a store migration or a Prefs change again.
  • Prefs builds its Appearance controls from the registry, for the session and per application, each showing the design default, the inherited session value and the application's override, and gains a terminal Colours group.
  • An agent can read exactly what any window draws and why, and change any style token or chrome colour for the session, one application or one window, and the terminal's colours for the session, under any design source.
